L1.rationale: Mechanism present but unproven over a cycle: ROIC 13.9% now (3 years above WACC) vs a 7.1% 10-year median; a rational three-player structure supplies the barrier, but it failed once against Jio and is shared; CAP 5-10 years; per-share compounding moderate (revenue/share 4.4% a year, BVPS 4.7%).

L2.rationale: Core India mobile is volume-saturated; 10-year revenue CAGR 8.1% (16% over 5 years from a trough, partly inorganic and FX); high-growth pockets (homes, data centres, Africa) are small or FX-exposed.

L3.rationale: A real pricing-cycle mechanism (three industry repairs, each +14-16% ARPU with ~90% flow-through; management says INR 300 ARPU is needed for adequate returns) but undated, Soft and partly priced, from a mid-cycle base with record margins; turnaround complete; SOTP gap immaterial.

L4.rationale: Options (data centres, NBFC, Airtel Money) are worth roughly INR 29-66 a share against INR 1,779 and are shared with minorities and the promoter; the outcome distribution is not venture-shaped.

L1.assessment: Long-duration FCFF DCF at an 11.03% WACC with one tariff round gives INR 1,306-1,509 (point 1,378); the price implies 14.4% revenue growth for 10 years or a ~9.9% cost of equity, i.e. a CAP beyond the 5-10 years the evidence supports. E[IRR] 6.2%; if the 10.9x multiple holds, ~hurdle.

L3.assessment: The base already carries one round; with two rounds (years 2 and 5) the DCF point is INR 1,519, still 17% below the price. Earnings floor at trough multiples INR 915-1,113 (stress 685-853). No measurable normalisation gap the market is missing.

dimensions.rationale: Through-cycle returns are below the cost of capital: 10-year median ROIC 7.1% (constant tax) / 8.2% (reported tax) vs 11.03% WACC, a -2.8 to -3.9 pp spread (guide band 30-44); only FY2026 clears WACC on a constant-tax basis. Scored at the top of the band because ROIC reached 13.9% in FY2026 and incremental ROIC on capital added since FY2021 is 23-28%, partly a recovery from a depressed base.

Narrow moat: an entry barrier from spectrum, network and capital in a consolidated three-private-player market (CR3 95.8%, HHI ~3,700), shared with Jio, plus a ~20% ARPU premium from customer mix. The barrier failed against a well-funded entrant in 2016 (India mobile segment result swung by -INR 18,508 cr). Airtel Business shows durable 18-25% segment returns. Industry now disciplined (three synchronised repairs).

Reachable market about 2x revenue: India access AGR ~INR 2.9 lakh cr annualised, of which Airtel already holds 39.7%, plus homes, enterprise, data centres and Africa. India mobile volume is saturated; growth is ARPU-led (4-5% organic per management) and capex is rising into data centres, so reinvestment returns on new adjacencies are unproven.

Quantitative guide gives 85-100 (10-year CFO/PAT 8.6x; FCF positive in 8 of 10 years), deviated one band down with reason: after spectrum, lease principal and interest, equity FCF was only 0.23x PAT over 10 years and 0.72x over 5; recurring 'exceptional' regulatory/FX charges equal 0.88x cumulative PAT; FY2025 headline PAT was ~48% one-offs. FY2026 equity FCF (INR 53,054 cr) is the first strong surplus.

Net debt/EBITDA 0.79x (1.40x incl. leases; 1.29x company basis), AAA/Stable domestic rating; guide band 75-89, one band down because interest coverage was 0.42x at the FY2019 trough and survival then required INR 39,181 cr of new equity. Debt is mostly fixed-rate, long-dated DoT instalments; 24-month maturities covered 0.86x by liquid resources.

Operational competence high (price war, AGR shock and 4G/5G executed; planned CEO succession), balance-sheet and dividend promises 6/6 delivered. Offsets: capex guidance overruns (median +18.6% since FY2023; 5G 'capex-neutral' claim failed), 56% share-count dilution since FY2016 to fund the trough, value-unlocking announcements withdrawn.

Reporting generally reliable (unmodified audit opinions FY2017-FY2026, auditor rotation on statutory limits); governance Clean/Standard: independent audit and nomination committees, zero promoter pledges in 39 quarters. Prevents higher: the ICIL/Airtel Africa related-party swap with an unresolved corporate-opportunity question, ICIL treated as not related under Ind AS 24, the Chairman's two-company pay, holdco reliance on Airtel dividends, the 2018 Payments Bank KYC penalty.

Several material exposures: regulatory discretion (AGR, spectrum pricing, recurring levy re-assessments, state support for Vodafone Idea, political salience of tariffs); Africa FX and country risk now ~79% owned; founder-succession key-person risk; satellite and FWA at the edges.

business_quality.prevents_higher: Through-cycle returns below the cost of capital (10-year median ROIC ~7-8% vs 11.03% WACC); a moat shared with Jio that failed once against a well-funded entrant; heavy per-share dilution in the last decade.
business_quality.could_lower: A renewed price war or failed tariff discipline after the Jio IPO; capex staying above ~25% of revenue into data centres at sub-WACC returns; adverse regulatory re-assessments; an Africa devaluation.
business_quality.evidence_to_change: FY2027 ROIC vs WACC; whether a tariff round arrives and holds; FY2027 capex and data-centre returns; ICIL swap documents.

dimensions.rationale: Revised base value (one tariff round in year 2, adopted after the adversarial review) INR 1,306-1,509, midpoint 1,407.5, vs price INR 1,778.70: margin of safety -26%; tool anchor, no deviation. Draft base (no round) was -43%.

E[IRR] 6.2% over 5 years on the revised scenario set vs an 11.68% hurdle (band 0 to H-4); tool anchor, no deviation. Cross-checks: return decomposition ~8%; if today's 10.9x multiple holds, ~10-14% (CIO-C059), i.e. at best about the hurdle.

P(permanent loss >=30% over 5 years) in the 10-20% part of the low band: needs a competitive reset (once-a-decade base rate) or a valuation bear case (20% probability, -33% to -41% incl. dividends). Lower within band because the failure-case loss is large.

DEVIATION from the tool (99): the tool compares undiscounted 5-year horizon values with today's price, so even the over-priced base case counts as upside. Measured against the price compounded at the hurdle, the probability-weighted excess/shortfall is 0.06 on the revised set (CIO-C057; VAL-C050 on the draft set); anchor band <0.8 interpolates to 2 (calc/cio_price_ladder_hurdle_adj.py). The adversarial review independently judged the deviation economically correct (BEAR-C090).

Reverse DCF: the price needs 14.4% revenue growth for 10 years, a 51.9% EBIT margin, or a 9.5% WACC; on the bull operating set the implied WACC is 11.3%, about the run's WACC. The price embeds roughly the bull case (band boundary 30).

A visible compounding engine (FY2026 equity FCF INR 53,054 cr; DPS INR 24, +50%) but the value-moving catalyst, a tariff round, is Soft, undated and partly priced (2024 round drew a -1.9% excess move).
Liquid (90-session ADTV ~INR 1,209 cr; reference position exits in ~0.002 days; G5 not triggered). Minor dilution risk: a history of share-based transactions (ICIL swap 2.35% in Q1FY2027).

Most material valuation inputs are primary and reconciled by the CIO (revenue base, net debt, shares, minorities via listed prices); the risk-free rate, ERP and beta rest on tier-5 sources, corroborated independently.

investment_attractiveness.prevents_higher: No margin of safety (-26% even with one tariff round in the base); E[IRR] 6.2% below an 11.68% hurdle and below the 7.38% 10-year G-Sec; the price embeds roughly the bull case and requires today's 10.9x multiple to hold just to earn about the hurdle.
investment_attractiveness.could_lower: Higher Indian rates; no tariff round through FY2028 with capex rising; a competitive reset; an Africa FX shock.
investment_attractiveness.evidence_to_change: A ~20-25% lower price (E[IRR] reaches the hurdle near INR 1,400); two tariff rounds within 24 months with no churn; evidence that capex intensity falls below 20% of revenue; a structurally lower Indian rate regime.

bear.drivers: Tariff repair stalls; growth 9%->5%; EBIT margin flat ~32-33%; no excess return in the terminal value.

base.drivers: Growth 12%->7% plus one realised tariff round in year 2 (+8% India mobile revenue); EBIT margin ~33.5%->37%+; terminal ROIC 14%; capex intensity elevated (sales-to-capital 1.5; at 1.0 the point falls to INR 1,266).

bull.drivers: Two tariff rounds plus adjacencies; growth 14%->8%; EBIT margin to 42%; terminal ROIC 18%.

decision_triggers.method: CIO hurdle-adjusted ladder (calc/cio_price_ladder_hurdle_adj.py, step INR 25): IA1 and IA2 from valuation_tools.py anchors; IA4 from asymmetry measured against the price compounded at the 11.68% hurdle (documented deviation); IA3 and IA5-IA8 held at scorecard values. Scenario inputs calc/cio_scenarios_inputs.json (base revised to one tariff round, CIO-C056). The unadjusted tool ladder (calc/cio_price_ladder.json) gives buy_below 1,225 and avoid_above 1,975.
decision_triggers.notes: Hypothetical triggers, not limit orders. IA5 is also price-sensitive (at ~INR 1,400 the price implies about the base case, IA5 50-69), so the buy trigger is conservative; re-run if evidence changes.
